question: For a child aged 1–5 years with severe Vitamin A deficiency presenting with corneal ulceration (xerophthalmia grade X2), the WHO recommended treatment is 2 lakh IU of Vitamin A orally on day 1, day 2, and day 14.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The WHO therapeutic schedule for severe Vitamin A deficiency in children over 1 year is 200,000 IU (2 lakh IU) orally on day 1, day 2, and day 14. Infants under 6 months receive 50,000 IU and those 6–12 months receive 1 lakh IU.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The WHO protocol for severe xerophthalmia (X2, X3A, X3B) in children 1–5 years is 200,000 IU on day 1, day 2, and at least 2 weeks later (day 14) — three doses in total.
